item.title: 'A lot of fuel in the system right now': Record rainfall fills up hydro lakes
item.description: Meridian spilled from both its Waitaki (pictured) and Waiau schemes throughout December and January. Photo: Meridian Energy A wet summer has kept Meridian's hydro storage lakes topped up, which could help keep power prices in check down the track.

item.title: Trash-tastrophe: Rubbish truck rollover blocks road
item.description: Emergency services at the scene of the accident. Photo: Stephen Jaquiery A road in Green Island was blocked by a rubbish truck which rolled onto its side spilling debris this afternoon.

item.title: Certainty of conviction put mosque terrorist 'between a rock and a rock'
item.description: Flowers at the gate of Al Noor Mosque following the March 15, 2019, terror attacks. Photo: File image/Getty By Tim Brown of RNZ

item.title: Aussie Liberals dump first female leader after nine months
item.description: Sussan Ley lasted just nine months as leader of the Liberal Party. Photo: North East CMA via Wikimedia Commons The Liberals' first female leader Sussan Ley will resign from parliament after she was knifed by conservative Angus Taylor nine months into the job.

item.title: Unease over Collins' rival-free appointment to top job
item.description: Judith Collins will remain an MP and continue to hold her portfolios until she moves to her new position as Law Commission president in the middle of the year. Photo: RNZ By Craig McCulloch of RNZ

item.title: Tourist numbers back to pre-pandemic levels thanks to Aussie surge
item.description: A Jetstar flight arrives in Dunedin from Coolangatta last year. Australia was the biggest source of visitors to New Zealand in 2025. Photo: Gregor Richardson Tourist arrivals topped 3.5 million for the first time since the Covid-19 pandemic, driven by a surge in Australian visitors.

item.title: Horse and trainer test positive for meth after race win
item.description: Ival Brownlee has been disqualified from racing for 18 months. Photo: Facebook A winning racehorse that tested positive for methamphetamine was likely contaminated with the drug by its trainer.

item.title: Flower show to display colour, creativeness
item.description: North Otago Horticultural Society president Christine Schaffer, in her home garden, prepares for the society’s summer flower show this weekend. PHOTO: JULES CHIN Colourful creativity will be on display this weekend when the North Otago Horticultural Society holds its annual summer flower show at the Scottish Hall in Oamaru.
